summary: Independent review of the managed-exit reason completeness control. TESTS ONLY (+87/-0, one file); no runtime behaviour changes, so this closes a VERIFICATION gap, not a defect. THE GAP IT CLOSES WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: on 2026-09-11 I promoted mutants from the focused suites to the FULL unit suite and confirmed that adding a brand-new managed-exit reason left every existing test green, because the only classifier test was a hand-typed table. I VERIFIED THE NEW CONTROL CAN COME OUT FALSE, which is the entire point of a tests-only PR: injecting a genuinely new reason at a real emit site (ref, tag = bid, 'CW_PANIC_EXIT') turns it RED with 'managed-exit reasons need classification', and the opposite direction — removing 'oms_v2_managed_exit:CW_FLIP' from the classifier set — also turns it RED. Both mutations were anchor-checked and py_compiled before the run, and the worktree verified clean afterwards. DESIGN IS RIGHT: the control derives the reason contract by AST from the _emit_v2_exit_on_loop CALL SITES rather than from the classifier it is testing, so it is not the tautology the previous hand-maintained table was; it resolves f-string templates for the {tag} and SCALE_{level} shapes; and anything it cannot statically resolve is added as 'unresolved:...' so it FAILS CLOSED rather than silently skipping. It also asserts that CW_TARGET and SCALE_* are actually EMITTED, so the non-protective allowlist cannot go stale, and that both classify as non-protective — codex-2 confirmed independently that profit-taking closes are deliberately non-protective because they are the redundant close this whole mechanism defers. SCOPE LIMIT STATED HONESTLY: the scan covers reasons passed to _emit_v2_exit_on_loop; a managed-exit reason emitted through some other call path would not be discovered. That is a reasonable boundary today because that helper is the single emit point, but it is the assumption to revisit if a second emit path is ever added. Controlled full unit pair: base 1940d46 is TREE-IDENTICAL to dcdacf9 which I had already measured, so the baseline applies directly — base 46 failed/3605 passed, head 46 failed/3606 passed, ZERO new failure names and ZERO fixed, compared as sorted sets. Ruff clean. Ancestor test PASS. Reviewer differs from the author. No findings; nothing withheld.
